record.paper_title: Mapping Class Group Factorizations and Symplectic 4-Manifolds: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Let delta be the boundary twist in Map_{g,n}. Given two factorizations of delta as products of positive Dehn twists along nonseparating curves in Map_{g,n}, suppose the total spaces of the corresponding Lefschetz fibrations have the same Euler characteristic and signature. Is it always possible to transform one factorization into the other by a sequence of Hurwitz moves and partial conjugations, where a partial conjugation conjugates a contiguous block of factors by a Dehn twist that commutes with the product of that block? Equivalently at the symplectic 4-manifold level, are compact integral symplectic 4-manifolds with the same c_1^2, c_2, [omega]^2, and c_1 dot [omega] related by Luttinger surgeries?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_{g,n}$ be a compact oriented surface of genus $g$ with $n$ boundary components, and let $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ denote its mapping class group (relative to the boundary). Write $\delta\in\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ for the product of right-handed Dehn twists along curves parallel to the $n$ boundary components (the "boundary twist"). A positive factorization of $\delta$ is an expression
$$\delta = \tau_{c_1}\tau_{c_2}\cdots\tau_{c_N},$$
where each $\tau_{c_i}$ is a right-handed Dehn twist along a nonseparating simple closed curve $c_i\subset\Sigma_{g,n}$. Each such factorization determines a genus-$g$ Lefschetz fibration over the disk (or sphere when $n=0$) with $n$ distinguished sections, hence a symplectic 4-manifold; its Euler characteristic $\chi$ and signature $\sigma$ are determined by the factorization.

Two elementary moves on positive factorizations are defined:
(i) a Hurwitz move replaces a pair $\tau_{c_i}\tau_{c_{i+1}}$ by $(\tau_{c_i}\tau_{c_{i+1}}\tau_{c_i}^{-1})\tau_{c_i} = \tau_{\tau_{c_i}(c_{i+1})}\tau_{c_i}$ or its inverse;
(ii) a partial conjugation replaces a contiguous block $\tau_{c_i}\tau_{c_{i+1}}\cdots\tau_{c_j}$ by $\phi\,\tau_{c_i}\cdots\tau_{c_j}\,\phi^{-1}$, where $\phi$ is a Dehn twist (or a product of Dehn twists arising from Luttinger surgery data) that commutes with $\tau_{c_i}\tau_{c_{i+1}}\cdots\tau_{c_j}$.

Question. Suppose two positive factorizations of $\delta$ in $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ by nonseparating Dehn twists give Lefschetz fibrations whose total spaces have the same Euler characteristic and the same signature. Must the two factorizations be related by a finite sequence of Hurwitz moves and partial conjugations?

Equivalently at the level of symplectic 4-manifolds: if $(X_1,\omega_1)$ and $(X_2,\omega_2)$ are compact integral symplectic 4-manifolds with equal Chern numbers $c_1^2$ and $c_2$, equal symplectic volumes $[\omega_i]^2$, and equal $c_1\cdot[\omega_i]$, must $X_2$ be obtainable from $X_1$ by a finite sequence of Luttinger surgeries along Lagrangian tori?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a well-known list of open problems posed by Auroux on factorizations in mapping class groups and Luttinger surgery equivalence of symplectic 4-manifolds. Subsequent work (e.g., unchaining surgery results and constructions of exotic 4-manifolds via Luttinger surgery) explores the conjecture but does not resolve it; nonminimal cases and general examples remain unclear, so the problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions about symplectic 4-manifolds, singular plane curves, and mapping class group factorizations
status_evidence.snippet: Auroux poses questions concerning whether positive factorizations giving Lefschetz fibrations with equal Euler characteristic and signature are related by Hurwitz moves and partial conjugations, equivalent to a Luttinger-surgery equivalence statement for integral symplectic 4-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open question by Auroux.

status_evidence.title: Unchaining surgery and topology of symplectic 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies surgeries on Lefschetz fibrations and symplectic 4-manifolds, building on but not resolving Auroux's Luttinger-equivalence conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature treats the question as still open.
